description: We are a group of high school students we are passionate about space and real world problems.
summary: With the changing climate and environment, it is getting harder for people to predict what is going to come next for their field. The real problem farmers face is that geting help is complicated and when you face complete giberish facts when you do it on your own let alone being sure that data you use is suitable for you. That's why we developed DECO (DEcision+CrOp), a bilingual public website that helps farmers anywhere to compare and decide crop rotations using NASA data easily. Users can pick a field on the map, replay 25 years of monthly NASA maps of vegetation, soil moisture, rain, temperature and groundwater, and enter their current rotation. DECO then scores that rotation and suggests new alternatives on six criteria: climate fit, water, nitrogen, soil cover, pest cycle and sellability (market advantage). The scores come from an algorithm that combines layers of data from reliable sources like NASA,FAO and even farmer's own answers via the forum section. Climate sliders let farmers test how rotations hold up to climate challenges and since we believe education is crucial, we offer understandable modules for farmers. DECO helps to make better-informed choices by real scientific data, and discuss it with a local adviser. There is also a demo part where feedback is collected from farmers by the "From the Field" forum and "My Field" where farmers can create profiles and track their field, enter data monthly, get personalized suggestions and yearly predictions.
details:
DECO is a crop rotation decision tool that runs in the browser at https://aleyna-dogan6d.github.io/DECO/. A farmer searches for a village or clicks the map anywhere on Earth. They can replay monthly NASA maps (vegetation greenness, soil and root-zone moisture, rain, air temperature and groundwater) to see how their area has changed since 2001. They then answer a few questions (soil, irrigation, slope, priorities, crops that sell easily locally) and enter their current rotation with sowing and harvest months.

DECO gathers climate data and compares it with each crop's temperature and rain ranges specific for the area chosen. It scores the farmer's rotation and offers new alternatives by ranking options from 1 to 5 on six criteria: climate fit, water, nitrogen (share of legumes), soil cover (how much rain falls on bare soil), pest cycle (same plant family back to back) and sellability (market advantage). Each alternative makes one change aimed at saving water, building soil health or selling more easily and the other rotations, seen when scrolled, offer new ideas. DECO also checks whether a different order or sowing month of the farmer's own crops would score better. Every card can be opened to show each criterion's score, the rule and the data behind it, risks, information gaps, and links to FAO and NASA resources. We also consider data given by the farmers which are collected by the forum and the short 5-minute-test taken by farmers guided by are system that gives simple instructions to follow which produces vital information for our predictions.

Climate sliders (0 to +3 °C, -30% to +10% rain) adjust effective rain using the FAO-56 Hargreaves method and re-score every card, so farmers can test a plan against a hotter, drier future. A prototype "My field" page saves a field and rotation in the browser, suggests this year's rotation and keeps monthly field notes.

Additionally, we believe that education is the hearth of development and understandable and relaible data should be available to everyone. That's why we have a short education part where there are modules explaining crop rotation, climate change etc. in the simpleset words while preserving it cruciality.

Good rotations protect soil, save water and break pest cycles, but most farmers choose by habit and few have access to climate data for their own field, even when they do they struggle to put this information into practical use. DECO puts free NASA data behind a simple, explainable comparison that works on a phone, for a farmer in Konya, Punjab, Kenya or Jamaica; simply everywhere on Earth.

HTML, CSS and JavaScript (static site, no server), Leaflet for maps, Chart.js for charts, GSAP for animation, Python to build the crop table from ECOCROP, GitHub Pages for hosting were the main tools of this project.

DECO starts from the farmer's own crops instead of a generic "best crop" list, shows 25 years of satellite history for any point on Earth, and lets the farmer test a plan against future climate scenarios. Every score is explainable in plain language. We also differ by visualizing the data and the time-laps in an attractive way, offering personalized features for users, including actual comments of farmers in to our predictions, giving simple explanations to users in addition to complex data and feeding farmers with diverse options for them to optimize their field accordingly to their needs ands wants while also considering nature and risks.
